newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent pares earlier gains in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent pares earlier gains in lacklustre trade.

text.p: IPE Brent futures pared earlier gains at midday on Friday as a corrective bounce lost momentum in a lacklustre market, traders said.
June Brent was trading 16 cents higher at $17.85 a barrel at 1206 GMT, off earlier highs of $17.93. It closed 12 cents lower on Thursday.
"It's just drifting off. There's a complete lack of interest at the moment," one trader said.
"It was helped up at the open by a bit of short-covering but it's pretty dull now," said another trader.
Few players expected the front-month to challenge the $18 mark during the session, let alone resistance at the double top at $18.50 and the gap at $18.62-77.

Gas oil, which led the market higher in earlier trade on the back of weather-related heat gains, also waned slightly. The May contract was 75 cents higher at $163.00 against the intra-day high of $163.75 a tonne.

Cold weather forecasts for the U.S. Northeast and Midwest boosted NYMEX heat by as much as 0.65 cent in ACCESS trading. It last traded a 0.30 cent higher at 54.30 a gallon. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
